title: ESP32 OTA: partitions and recovery from a failed update

spans.text: For safer ESP32 updates, flash can hold the running application and another app slot. The new image is written to the inactive slot; after reboot, the device performs basic health checks. If they pass, the new image is confirmed. If it cannot start correctly, the bootloader can return to the previous working slot.

`esp_ota_get_running_partition()` finds the active slot; `ESP_OTA_IMG_PENDING_VERIFY` means the new image is still on trial. This example checks the partition and API results. Call `confirmPendingImage(true)` only after essential health checks pass; `false` requests rollback and reboot. The caller must also inspect the confirmation API's return value.

This is an ESP-IDF API and may be exposed by Arduino-ESP32, but do not assume it works in a plain Arduino sketch without configuration. The partition table, rollback option, and image verification must agree. Start from Espressif's official OTA example for ESP-IDF projects.

spans.title: Important note
spans.text: Confirm the image only after real sensor, storage, and communication checks pass. Changing the partition table can erase flash data; prepare a backup and recovery method first.
